theme: Consumer credit and BNPL: Klarna/Affirm public stats, Fed G.19, credit card delinquency, CFPB complaints dataset (Airbnb refund complaints), BBB complaint scrapers

candidates.name: cfpb/consumer-credit-trends-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Official CFPB repo backing the 'Consumer Credit Trends' site. Committed CSV files (plus JSON used by cfpb-chart-builder) split into four market folders: auto-loans, credit-cards, mortgages, student-loans. Each market has origination counts and dollar volumes, YoY % changes, state-level annual changes, and demographic cuts (borrower age, credit score tier, neighborhood income). Many series indexed to Jan-2009 baseline; monthly cadence; updated as recently as 2 Sep 2026 per repo activity. No stars/license metadata surfaced but repo is under the official cfpb GitHub org (public-domain CC0 pattern used by other cfpb repos).
candidates.why_useful: Direct, free, monthly, point-in-time-able proxy for US consumer credit health (credit-card originations/credit tightness) — feeds the 'consumer strength' driver in the ABNB nights/ADR model and is a genuine Fed/CFPB-adjacent consumer credit series (gap area: consumer credit/BNPL theme; adjacent to gap #6 consumer spend panels). Credit-card credit tightness and delinquisyncratic segments could be tested as a leading indicator for discretionary travel spend.
candidates.time_coverage: index base Jan 2009 to present, monthly
candidates.size_hint: multiple CSV/JSON files across 4 market folders, unknown total row count

candidates.name: MarkPhamm/local_warehouse_pipeline
candidates.what_it_holds: A local-first ELT pipeline (dlt + PyArrow extraction, DuckDB + dbt transform, Prefect orchestration, Visivo dashboards) that pulls CFPB consumer-complaint data live from the CFPB complaints API. Users configure target companies and start dates in src/cfg/config.py; staged data lands as daily Parquet files under landing/cfpb_complaints/YYYY_MM_DD/, one file per company per day, supporting incremental and historical backfills. MIT-licensed, updated 27 Jun 2026, 11 stars.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made, working, non-Airbnb-site method to pull CFPB complaint records filtered to a target company — pointed at 'Airbnb, Inc.' as the configured company this becomes exactly the sanctioned CFPB-complaints-about-Airbnb dataset the theme asks for (refund/cancellation complaint counts and text as a service-friction proxy), without scraping airbnb.com itself.
candidates.time_coverage: configurable start date to present, daily granularity
candidates.size_hint: pipeline code, not a static dataset; output scales with configured pull window

candidates.name: PratikshPandita/consumer-complaint-root-cause-analytics
candidates.what_it_holds: SQL/Python analytics repo built on the public CFPB consumer-complaints dataset, using BigQuery for root-cause trend analysis plus a validation framework for a text-classification model's output. Updated 13 Sep 2026 (same day as this scout run), 0 stars, no license listed.
candidates.why_useful: Shows a working BigQuery-based ingestion/query pattern against the full CFPB complaints public dataset (which is queryable by company name, so 'Airbnb' complaints could be isolated); useful as a template method even though it ships no committed Airbnb-specific extract.
candidates.time_coverage: whatever the CFPB complaints dataset covers (2011-present)
candidates.size_hint: code only, queries live BigQuery public dataset

candidates.name: daguar/cfpb-consumer-complaints-database
candidates.what_it_holds: Old (2013) 'meeting ground' repo — no committed data or scraper, just a discussion hub pointing users to the official CFPB Consumer Complaints database at the Socrata portal data.consumerfinance.gov and its API. 4 stars, last updated 2013, no data files.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the canonical free source for CFPB complaints (data.consumerfinance.gov Socrata API, filterable by company='AIRBNB' and product/issue) that any of the other repos in this list, or a fresh one-off pull, would hit; low value on its own since it holds nothing.

candidates.name: ud4yfr/bnpl-stress-test
candidates.what_it_holds: Monte Carlo stress-test model comparing Affirm vs Klarna unit economics under rising delinquency scenarios. Appears to be a modeling exercise (parametrized assumptions), not a committed real-data extract of Affirm/Klarna disclosed statistics. Updated 1 Aug 2026, 0 stars, no license listed.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: illustrates how BNPL delinquency sensitivity could be modeled, but does not appear to hold real disclosed Affirm/Klarna public stats (10-Q GMV, delinquency rates) that would be the actual high-value target; would need inspection of source code to confirm any embedded real figures.

candidates.name: VenkataVarshiniC/BNPL-project
candidates.what_it_holds: A BNPL default-modeling project framed around a single question a company like Klarna/Affirm would ask (transaction fees vs default losses). Updated 13 Sep 2026, 0 stars, no license. Likely uses a synthetic or Kaggle-style loan dataset rather than real Klarna/Affirm disclosures — not confirmed without deeper inspection.
candidates.why_useful: Low-confidence lead; flagged for completeness under the BNPL keyword but unlikely to carry real, usable Klarna/Affirm public statistics without further checking file contents.

gh search repos "cfpb consumer complaints dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "consumer credit delinquency federal reserve" --sort stars
gh search repos "bnpl buy now pay later dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "G.19 consumer credit" --sort stars
gh search repos "credit card delinquency rate dataset" --sort stars
notes: Direct keyword searches for 'CFPB complaints airbnb', 'bnpl usage data', 'consumer credit data', 'G.19 consumer credit', and 'credit card delinquency rate dataset' all returned ZERO results via gh search repos (the GitHub repo-search API does not full-text-index README content well and these multi-word queries are too specific). Broader single/double-word queries (cfpb, affirm-klarna) surfaced real hits. Nobody appears to have mirrored the Fed's actual G.19 consumer credit release or Klarna/Affirm's own quarterly disclosed stats (GMV, delinquency %) as a committed GitHub dataset — those numbers live in Klarna's/Affirm's own investor-relations PDFs and the Fed's G.19 release (federalreserve.gov/releases/g19), not GitHub; a FRED API pull (series e.g. DRCCLACBS, TERMCBCCALLNS) would be the more direct free path and is arguably already covered by the team's existing FRED holdings per CONTEXT.md rather than a GitHub-native find. The strongest real find is cfpb/consumer-credit-trends-data (official, live-updated, monthly, state-level credit-card/auto/mortgage origination and credit-tightness data) plus MarkPhamm/local_warehouse_pipeline as a working, configurable puller of CFPB complaints filtered by company name — pointed at 'Airbnb' this is the closest thing to a ready CFPB-Airbnb-complaints acquisition method found. No BBB complaint scraper repos surfaced in any query. Did not use gh search code (0/1 budget used) or gh api contents calls (0/8 used) since README fetches via raw.githubusercontent.com answered the needed questions without API cost.
